terms.definition: Rock formed by the cooling and solidifying of molten materials.
Rock that has formed through the deposition and solidification of sediment, especially sediment transported by water, ice, and wind.
Rock that was once one form of rock but has changed to another under the influence of heat, pressure, or some other agent without passing through a liquid phase.
Hot fluid or semifluid material below or within the earth's crust from which lava and other igneous rock is formed by cooling.
The breaking down of rocks, soil, and minerals as well as wood and artificial materials through contact with the Earth's atmosphere, waters, and biological organisms.
The process by which soil and rock particles are worn away and moved elsewhere by gravity, or by a moving transport agent – wind, water, or ice.
A distinct layer of soil parallel to the land surface whose physical, chemical, and biological characteristics differ from layers above and beneath it.
Dark, organic material formed in soil by the microbial decomposition of plant and animal matter, essential for soil fertility and water retention.
The solid, rocky component of Earth, encompassing the crust, mantle, and core, as well as surface rocks, sediments, and soils.
The combined mass of water found on, under, and over the surface of a planet, including oceans, glaciers, freshwater bodies, groundwater, and atmospheric vapor.
The protective layer of gases surrounding a planet held in place by gravity, shielding against cosmic radiation and regulating surface temperature.
The global ecological system integrating all living organisms and their relationships, extending across the geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere.
